subject: Bridgestone service impact: sticky NAT translation flap causing tail latency and 502s
messages:
From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@bridgestone.com>
To: support@redwood.ai; marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Bridgestone Network Ops <netops@bridgestone.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: [Bridgestone] Intermittent 502s and tail latency on inference calls

Hi Marcus / Redwood support,

We're seeing a sustained regression in tail latency and an increase in 502s for all model endpoints proxied through the Portland colo peering link. The issue started Friday evening and has worsened this morning — P95/P99 token latency jumped ~4-6x and throughput for our production workload dropped by ~30%. Our telemetry shows repeated connection resets and what looks like NAT port churn on the path to Redwood's edge (we're seeing many ephemeral port reassignments in our gateway logs).

Attached are a short log slice and a capture showing frequent TCP RSTs between our edge NAT and Redwood's peering endpoint. Can you confirm whether there were any changes on Redwood's side (proxy config, firewall rewrite rules, or peering maintenance) in the last 36 hours? This is customer-facing and impacting checkout flows — we need an ETA and a mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Carlos
Network Reliability Engineer
Bridgestone Payments

Attachment stubs: bridgestone-logs-11-20.zip (30MB), pcap-sample-11-21.txt (4MB)

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@bridgestone.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Bridgestone] Intermittent 502s and tail latency on inference calls

Carlos — thanks for the clear notes and capture. We're escalating to infra immediately.

Short answers up front: no planned peering maintenance on our side over the weekend, and no recent firewall rule pushes in the affected region. That said, symptoms (ephemeral port churn, RSTs, frequent TCP session churn) point at a translation/NAT boundary or intermediate proxy rebalancer.

Action items I am putting in motion now:
- Infra (Rishi): collect NAT session metrics, proxy pool health, and VPC peering route table snapshots for Portland -> us-west-2.
- Networking (Vanessa): review upstream peering health and request a circulation check with our colo partner.
- Account: I'll coordinate an exec sync with Bridgestone leadership if we can't stabilize in 24h.

Please keep pcap/log slices coming — those are most helpful. I'll follow up with a short incident timeline and mitigation plan within 2 hours.

-Marcus Lin
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0189

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai; grace.oconnor@redwood.ai; vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@bridgestone.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 11:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Bridgestone] Intermittent 502s and tail latency on inference calls

On Mon, Nov 22, 2027 at 09:25 Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Carlos — thanks for the clear notes and capture. We're escalating to infra immediately.

Preliminary triage notes (quick dump):
- We pulled NAT translation counters from the Portland peering colo (our edge node) and see repeated 5–10s bursts of ephemeral port reassignments on the public NAT gateway handling Bridgestone connections. That matches the RSTs in the pcap and the customer telemetry.
- Proxy pool logs show continuous TCP reconnects; connection pooling is healthy but sessions are being torn because port mappings are flapping.
- VPC peering (route table) looks stable from our side; BGP flaps not observed in that time window.
- DNS: we saw a handful of short TTL-resolves but nothing that would explain session churn — worth monitoring.

Likely root cause hypothesis: partner colo NAT (sticky NAT translation) is aggressively rebalancing sessions when their aggregation layer experiences transient overload, causing session ID changes and downstream proxies to see new 5-tuple mappings -> resulting in tokenization/timeouts and 502s at the app layer.

Short-term mitigations (we can implement within 1–3 hours):
1) Force a different egress IP from our edge for Bridgestone traffic (route hold/steer) to avoid the overloaded NAT.
2) Enable connection draining on the proxy pool for sessions from Bridgestone to avoid mid-session tears.
3) Coordinate with Bridgestone NetOps to increase NAT port pool or relax sticky timeout on their gateway (they control the NAT) — request already sent.

I've opened INF-7124 and uploaded the nat-summary-20271122.csv and a sampled pcap. Next steps: I'll attempt the egress steer now and report results in 20–30 minutes. If steering does not reduce resets, we should plan an exec sync and temporary credit for impacted calls.

Rishi Malhotra
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: nat-summary-20271122.csv, pcap-sample-11-21.txt

From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@bridgestone.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai; rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai; vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Ibarra <elena.ibarra@bridgestone.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 07:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Bridgestone] Intermittent 502s and tail latency on inference calls

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the rapid triage. We just confirmed with our colo partner that there were two transient control-plane reconfig events around 03:40 and 05:10 PST which coincided with the highest error spikes. They believe the sticky-NAT balancing threshold is throwing sessions around when the aggregation layer briefly reports high CPU. They've proposed a temporary NOS config to enlarge the ephemeral port range and increase sticky timeout.

We're happy to coordinate on the steer you mentioned — please share the target egress IP and any expected client-side implications. Also, because this impacted our peak checkout window yesterday, our ops director (Elena) is requesting a timeline to resolution and would like to escalate to an exec call if we can't achieve full mitigation within 12 hours.

Our business asks: clear communication on mitigation steps, a postmortem outlining root cause and prevention, and a credit for the degraded 48h window.

Carlos

On Tue, Nov 23, 2027 at 07:48 Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@bridgestone.com> wrote:

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-leadership@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Nov 2027 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Executive brief: Bridgestone incident — NAT translation churn at partner edge, proposed customer remedies

Team — brief summary and recommended ask for leadership approval:

Summary:
- Impact: Bridgestone observed P99 latency increases (4–6x) and a sustained 502 spike across inference endpoints between 2027-11-20T03:30 and 2027-11-23T10:00 PST, reducing throughput ~30% during peak traffic.
- Root cause: sticky NAT translation rebalancing at the partner colo aggregation layer caused ephemeral port remapping and mid-session tears. No config push from Redwood; this was triggered by spiky CPU on partner side when aggregation autoscaling failed to react in time.
- Mitigation already executed: Rishi performed an egress steer to alternate edge IP (reduced resets by ~90%), enabled connection draining on proxy pool, and coordinated a temporary port-range increase with Bridgestone NetOps. INF-7124 created and updated.

Customer asks / business impact:
- Bridgestone requests a 48h service credit window and an exec sync (they requested escalation if not stabilized within 12h).
- Potential upsell/renewal risk if the postmortem and remediation plan are not shared promptly.

Recommended leadership actions:
1) Approve a customer service credit for the impacted 48-hour window (estimate impact = ~12% of November hosted usage for this account).
2) Join an executive sync with Bridgestone on Wednesday 2027-11-30 at 10:00 PST to present the postmortem and roadmap for safeguards (we'll invite Infra, Networking, and Account execs).
3) Sponsor a short-term audit of our edge NAT provisioning and partner SLAs for sticky NAT behaviour (one-week runway for findings).

I recommend approving the credit and committing an exec to the sync. If approved, I'll confirm language and send the calendar invite to Bridgestone (Carlos + Elena).

Thanks — Marcus
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
